title: Village of Lyubavichi Today
caption: The village of Lyubavichi as it appears today — a quiet settlement in the Smolensk region that was once the heart of Chabad-Lubavitch for 102 years.
description: Lyubavichi (Lubavitch) is a village in Rudnyansky District, Smolensk Oblast, Russia. For 102 years (1813–1916) it served as the spiritual center of the worldwide Chabad-Lubavitch movement.
alt: Aerial view of Lyubavichi village, Smolensk Oblast, Russia

title: The Schneerson House
caption: The Schneerson House in Lyubavichi — purchased in 1989 and registered in the name of the Lubavitcher Rebbe. Today it serves as a guest house and museum for visitors.
description: This building was acquired in 1989 and is registered in the name of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson. It serves as a hospitality center and small museum documenting Chabad history in Lubavitch.

title: Ohel of the Tzemach Tzedek and Rebbe Maharash
caption: The Ohel covering the resting places of the Tzemach Tzedek (1789–1866) and the Rebbe Maharash (1834–1882) — the central pilgrimage site of Lubavitch.
description: The Ohel of the Rebbeim is the central sacred site of Lubavitch. The third and fourth Chabad Rebbeim are buried here. The structure was rebuilt in 1989 and renovated in 2023–2024.
alt: Ohel of the founders of the Lubavitch Hasidic branch

title: Cemetery and Ohel Grounds
caption: The restored grounds of the Lubavitch cemetery. Spanning approximately 70 by 150 meters, it contains around 200 preserved Hebrew-inscribed monuments.
description: The historic cemetery of Lubavitch. Restoration work beginning in 1989 and continuing through the 2020s has uncovered and reinstalled hundreds of matzeivos.
alt: Graves and Ohel area at Lubavitch cemetery

title: Matzeivos at the Lubavitch Cemetery
caption: Historic matzeivos in the Lubavitch cemetery. Over 200 Hebrew-inscribed monuments have been preserved and hundreds more uncovered during the restoration project.
description: During the Geder Avos restoration project (2018–present), hundreds of tombstones were uncovered, cleaned, and reinstalled in their proper locations. A complete database of every grave has been compiled.

title: The Alter Rebbe — Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi
caption: Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi (1745–1812), founder of Chabad-Lubavitch and author of the Tanya. His son the Mitteler Rebbe established Lubavitch as the movement's center in 1813.
description: The Alter Rebbe founded Chabad-Lubavitch in the late 18th century. His magnum opus, the Tanya, remains the foundational philosophical text of Chabad to this day.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Schneur Zalman of Liadi, the Alter Rebbe, founder of Chabad-Lubavitch

title: The Mitteler Rebbe — Rabbi Dovber Schneuri
caption: Rabbi Dovber Schneuri (1773–1827), second Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. He settled in Lubavitch around 1813, establishing the village as the center of the movement for the next century.
description: The Mitteler Rebbe led Chabad following his father and was responsible for making Lubavitch the movement's home. He systematized the practice of Chassidic contemplation.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Dovber Schneuri, the Mitteler Rebbe

title: The Tzemach Tzedek — Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn
caption: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn (1789–1866), the third Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, known as the Tzemach Tzedek. He led the movement for nearly 40 years from Lubavitch and is buried there.
description: The Tzemach Tzedek led Chabad from 1827 until his passing in Lubavitch in 1866. His Ohel in Lubavitch remains one of the central sites of pilgrimage in the Chabad world.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneersohn, the Tzemach Tzedek

title: The Rebbe Maharash — Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn
caption: Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn (1834–1882), fourth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. He led from Lubavitch and is buried there alongside the Tzemach Tzedek.
description: The Rebbe Maharash was the seventh son of the Tzemach Tzedek and led Chabad for over two decades. He is known for his teaching 'l'chatchilah ariber' — start from above.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Shmuel Schneersohn, the Rebbe Maharash

title: The Rebbe Rashab — Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn
caption: Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn (1860–1920), fifth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. In 1897 he founded Yeshivah Tomchei Temimim in Lubavitch, the first yeshiva to integrate deep Talmud and Chassidus study.
description: The Rebbe Rashab led Chabad from Lubavitch and founded Tomchei Temimim, the yeshiva that shaped the character of Chabad education for all subsequent generations.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Sholom Dovber Schneersohn, the Rebbe Rashab

title: The Frierdiker Rebbe — Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn
caption: Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn (1880–1950), sixth Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch, born in Lubavitch. He delivered his last Maamar in Russia here in 1922 before eventually emigrating westward.
description: The Frierdiker Rebbe was born in Lubavitch and led Chabad through some of its darkest periods. He built the institutional foundation for the worldwide Chabad expansion that would follow.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Yosef Yitzchak Schneersohn, the Frierdiker Rebbe

title: The Lubavitcher Rebbe — Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson
caption: Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson (1902–1994), seventh Rebbe of Chabad-Lubavitch. Under his leadership Chabad expanded to over 100 countries and thousands of communities worldwide.
description: The Lubavitcher Rebbe accepted the nesius in 1951 and transformed Chabad into a worldwide movement. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential Jewish figures of the 20th century.
alt: Portrait of Rabbi Menachem Mendel Schneerson, the Lubavitcher Rebbe
